searchText: Will ETH2 use keccak256 for its standard hashing algorithm, or SHA3? **vbuterin** Sha256 SHA-256, not SHA3-256? **dankrad** Yes Interesting. For the performance benefit I assume? Mainly interoperability considerations. Background is here: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/pull/779 And here: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/612 so having a situation like we had with the roughtime bug, what happens when people decide their penalty for turning off their validators is safer than getting slashed? and an even more abstract question, what happens when an unforeseen bug causes a small but not insignificant amount of validators to become slashed, for no fault of their own? do we risk jeopardizing trust in eth because of the anti evangelizing that might come out of such a scenario?
